sources.entry: musikcube - Streaming audio server with Linux/macOS/Windows/Android clients. BSD-3-Clause C++/deb

summary.one_liner: musikcube is a cross-platform, terminal-based audio engine, library, player and streaming audio server written in C++.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes musikcube as a terminal-based audio player and library that compiles on Windows, macOS and Linux and runs on Raspberry Pi. It can run as a streaming audio server: a websocket server on port 7905 handles metadata retrieval and remote control, and an HTTP server on port 7906 serves optionally transcoded audio to clients. The README mentions an Android client called musikdroid that can stream from and remote control musikcube. Installation options named include releases binaries, Homebrew, FreeBSD pkg, OpenBSD pkg_add and Chocolatey. The README also lists supported decoders, audio outputs (ALSA, PulseAudio, PipeWire, CoreAudio, WASAPI, DirectSound, WaveOut) and a UI built on ncurses or PDCurses.
use_cases: play local music library from the terminal
stream audio from a home server to other devices
remote control a music player from an Android phone
run a music player on a Raspberry Pi connected to a stereo
self-host a music streaming server on a local network
manage and tag a music library in the console
notable: Terminal-based player and library that runs on Windows, macOS, Linux and Raspberry Pi
Built-in streaming audio server with websocket metadata API and HTTP audio serving, enabled by default
Android companion app musikdroid can stream and remote control the player
Broad audio output support including ALSA, PulseAudio, PipeWire, CoreAudio, WASAPI
Packaged for Homebrew, Chocolatey, FreeBSD and OpenBSD
caveats: The README says the server and remote API should not be considered safe outside a local network: websocket auth is a simple password challenge, HTTP uses only Basic auth, and there is no SSL/TLS (a reverse proxy is suggested for SSL termination).
The server stores the password in plain text in a local settings file.
The Android client is a separate app (musikdroid) referenced by the README.
keywords: stream my music to my phone
